findings.title: `report history` requires git, contradicting the "No git" module contract and lacking its own data flow and failure modes
findings.description: The Component Structure table states the three report assembly modules — including `history_report.py` — have "No git and no store writes beyond what `ensure_snapshot` and `record_slice_ranges` do" (line 99). But the API Contracts section specifies `report history` orders snapshots "by the target's first-parent history" (line 298), which can only come from `git log --first-parent <target>` — stored `CodeSnapshot` records carry a commit SHA, not parent links. The Data Flow section gives flows for range resolution, export and `report slice` only; `report project` and `report history` have none, so the git dependency (whose source, injection and error handling are unspecified) is hidden. This matters because the failure-mode table's git entries cover `git archive`, `rev-parse`, reflog and merge searches — not a first-parent history query, so a `run_git` timeout or missing target ref in `report history` has no stated handling. Relatedly, line 298 places review findings "on the row of the landing's `after_sha`", which presupposes history reads (or resolves) slice ranges — also unstated. Fix: either state that `history_report` takes the first-parent list as an injected argument (keeping "no git" true at the assembly layer, with the CLI command supplying it and handling a `None` from `run_git`), or amend the table and add history's failure rows and data flow.

findings.title: `resolve_diff_base`'s silent degrade-to-`main` can persist a wrong landing in a record that is never corrected
findings.description: The data flow uses `target = resolve_diff_base(repo_root)` annotated "(git.integration_branch, or main)". Verified in `src/squadron/review/git_utils.py:340-380`: `resolve_diff_base` returns `DEFAULT_DIFF_BASE = "main"` whenever `cf` is unavailable, the read fails, or the key is unset — a silent fallback. D2 rejects `_find_merge_commit`'s `main` fallback precisely because it "isn't [acceptable] for a record that's kept forever," and D1 makes stored landings append-only and immutable ("stored ones never change", "A wrong landing stays in the store" — Risk Assessment). The same rationale applies to the target ref: on a project with `git.integration_branch` where `cf` is temporarily unavailable, a resolution run under `target=main` can record a landing (or a `NO_LANDING`-driven fast-forward resolution) against the wrong branch's first-parent line, permanently — and it also violates the project rule "Never use silent fallback values." The `target_ref` field makes it visible after the fact but not correctable. Fix: for the durable `slice-ranges`/`report slice` path, resolve the target strictly (following 196's `read_integration_target` precedent — a `cf` failure raises rather than degrading) or at minimum refuse to persist when the target was obtained by fallback, logging the reason as an unresolved state.

findings.title: `compute_delta` and `is_within_floor` come from 324, not 323
findings.description: The Prerequisites line attributes `baseline_report`, `compute_delta` and `is_within_floor` to "323 (complete)". `baseline_report` is 323's (`src/squadron/metrology/audit_report.py:54`), but `compute_delta` and `is_within_floor` are 324's additions (`src/squadron/metrology/audit_delta.py:38-100`). 324 is also complete, so there is no dependency risk — but line 326 ("323: `baseline_report` and `compute_delta`, unchanged") repeats the misattribution in the Consumes section and would send a task-time reader to the wrong document.
